newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Virgin Express says would not split buy order.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Express says would not split buy order.

text.p: Virgin Express, the cut-price airline operation of Richard Branson's Virgin Group , will get all the 25 new planes it is looking to buy from one maker, the firm's chief financial officer said on Wednesday.
"It will be all or nothing. We would never split the order," James Swigart told Reuters.

He confirmed a report in Wednesday's Wall Street Journal that Virgin Express, which is headquartered in Brussels, was negotiating with Boeing, Airbus Industrie and McDonnell Douglas Corp, but said there was still some way to go in the talks.
"It is not days. It is unlikely to be weeks. It is certainly not imminent," Swigart said.
He said one of the options the firm had was simply to decide not to buy now and instead to continue leasing.
"The average age of our fleet is only about five years. We will only buy if we can make good economic sense of it," Swigart said.

The list price of the new planes is $40 million each, which would make a total bill of $1.0 billion. But Swigart pointed out that bulk purchasers never paid face value, and the final bill was likely to be somewhat lower.
"Nevertheless it will still be a big figure...and we would still have to raise capital," Swigart said.
